text.p: Mexican telephone company Telefonos de Mexico SA (Telmex) on Monday reported 1996 net earnings of 11.60 billion pesos versus a 1995 net of 11.88 billion pesos.

The company's 1996 earnings per ADR was $3.34, or 1.27 pesos per local share. Telmex's 1995 earnings per local share was 1.17 pesos per share, according to information from the Mexican Stock Exchange (Bolsa).
During the fourth quarter alone, Telmex registered net profits of 83 million pesos, compared to 1.237 billion pesos during the last quarter of 1995, Telmex said in a statement.

Telmex took a one-time goodwill write-off of 1.561 billion pesos during the fourth quarter related to acquisitions the company made a few years ago. It also registered a non-recurring charge of 895 million pesos for expenses related to the opening of long distance services to competition.
On a per ADR basis, Telmex's earnings for the fourth quarter was $0.03.
The telephone company said its accumulated lines in service grew 0.3 percent in 1996 to 8,826,148 lines.
Total revenues for the fourth quarter rose to 13.558 billion pesos, a 9.3 percent increase versus the same period of 1995. Revenues for the year fell one percent, however, to 52.714 billion.

During the quarter, Telmex saw a 26.2 percent increase in domestic long distance revenues and a 14.7 percent increase in local service revenues. International long distance revenues fell 6.2 percent, however, mainly due to lower settlement rates with U.S. operators.

Domestic long distance traffic volume during the last three months of the year rose to 1.972 billion minutes versus 1.903 billion minutes in the fourth quarter of 1995. International long distance volume rose to 911 million minutes, up 14.4 percent versus the same period of 1995.
For the year, domestic long distance volume rose to 7.867 billion minutes, up 7.9 percent on 1995 levels. International long distance volume rose 16.2 percent from 1995 to 3.513 billion minutes.
Cash operating expenses for the quarter were 5.935 billion pesos, up 25.8 percent in real terms compared to the fourth quarter of 1995.
"This increase is mainly, besides the non-recurring charges...due to higher bad debt charges, advertising expenses and expenses related to the telephone network maintenance," Telmex said.
Aside from the goodwill write off and the expenses for long distance competition, Telmex also took a fourth quarter charge of 249 million pesos for charitable contributions.
Operating income for the quarter fell 3.3 percent to 4.855 billion pesos. For the year, Telmex's operating income fell by 14.1 percent to 20.250 billion pesos.
Telmex said it ended the year with 8,874,557,648 shares outstanding versus 9,681,411,562 at the end of 1995.
Telmex boosted the number of cellular telephone customers by 64.6 percent in 1996 to 656,723. Its Telcel cellular phone unit's revenue increased by 1.2 percent to 2.734 billion pesos for the year.

However, Telcel had an operating loss of 99 million pesos for the year versus an operating gain of 153 million pesos in 1995. Telmex said this was due to higher charges for fraudulent calls, increments of some operating costs and higher reserves for bad debts.
